title: VLD-01/02/03 implementation: validateDefinition returns findings on clean definitions (4 fail + 2 crash in src/validation/*.zig)
summary: On feature/wf02-vld01-03-20260816 @ 31482edb, `zig build test` reports 4 failing + 2 crashing in-file unit tests, all inside src/validation/. The strongest signal is the clean-path test `mod.test.validateDefinition: clean linear definition with one guard`, which expects 0 findings but observes 3 — the validator emits false positives on a definition that should be valid. The helper modules (site, pd06, typecheck) also fail their own unit tests with runtime panics/assertions, so the validation route wired in 31482edb (src/api/routes/validation.zig) cannot deliver the VLD-01/02/03 acceptance criteria end-to-end. Unit test gate is RED; this blocks the VLD-01/02/03 release.
scope: Implementation defect in the Stage 16 semantic validation modules under src/validation/ (site enumeration, PD-06 syntax check, CEL type check, and the aggregating validateDefinition entry point).

description: The Stage 16 semantic validation implementation landed in commit 31482edb does not satisfy its own in-file unit tests. Three distinct symptom clusters: (A) src/validation/site.zig — enumerateSites panics/asserts on gateway edge conditions, timer delays, and form visible_when/computed_from sites, so site enumeration does not produce the expected Site set. (B) src/validation/pd06.zig — runSyntaxCheck does not surface CEL_SYNTAX_INVALID for a malformed per-site expression. (C) src/validation/typecheck.zig — checkSite fails to report UnknownVariable for an unknown identifier and OperandTypeError for '+' over number and string. These three helper defects propagate into src/validation/mod.zig, where validateDefinition (i) reports 3 findings on a definition that should yield 0, (ii) does not produce the expected UnknownVariable finding for an unknown guard identifier, (iii) does not populate pd06_diagnostics for a malformed CEL guard, and (iv) does not order findings by (node_id, expression_path). The false-positive clean-path result is the strongest signal and should be diagnosed first, since it likely shares a root cause with the site-enumeration defects.
investigation_notes: Bench environment was verified HEALTHY by TEST-RUNNER before the run: `zig build test-env-verify` exit 0 (`verify_test_env: HEALTHY — 10 checks passed`), migrations 147/147 applied, schema baseline matches migrations/, no stale locks (C6), no config drift (C9). Therefore this is NOT an ENV_ISSUE. A second, independent blocker was reported in the same test report and is deliberately NOT part of this issue: the spec's integration test files tests/integration/validation_vld_unit_test.zig and tests/integration/validation_vld_http_test.zig do not exist on the branch or in git history (SPEC_DEVIATION → routes back to TEST-DESIGNER). Because those files are absent, spec coverage is 0/15 and the VLD acceptance criteria have no end-to-end evidence either way; this issue is scoped strictly to the implementation defects observable from the in-file unit tests.

The clean-path failure reproduces deterministically as `mod.test.validateDefinition: clean linear definition with one guard -> expected 0, found 3`.

actions: The validator entry point validateDefinition must never report findings on the clean/happy path - a valid definition must yield 0 findings; the clean-path test is authoritative and must return 0 findings before merge.
In-file unit tests for src/validation/* are authoritative - any new validation module must ship with its own passing in-file unit tests, and the clean-path test must return 0 findings before merge.

Memory ownership in src/validation/* must match the documented contract: freeSites owns and frees the whole []Site backing returned by enumerateSites' toOwnedSlice; TypedEnv ownership (who frees entries) must be explicit in test scaffolding; per-site []Finding backings from checkSite's toOwnedSlice must be freed to keep std.testing.allocator leak detection green.

The PD-06 per-site syntax gate must use the real expr.parse check (not delimiter-balance-only) so truncated/dangling-operator expressions are rejected and the VLD-02 AC4 short-circuit fires; run the PD-06 gate before any env-level finding is accumulated so the 'findings stays empty' contract holds.
The declared-type table (mapDeclaredTypeName) must map every CEL type name used in fixtures (including 'number') so no spurious UnknownVariableType / UnknownVariable false positive is emitted.

per_test.test: site.test.enumerateSites: gateway edge condition -> one Site per edge
per_test.root_cause: Memory leak, not logic: enumerateSites returns sites.toOwnedSlice(allocator); freeSites frees the per-site strings but never the []Site backing slice, so std.testing.allocator panics at test teardown ('leaked 1 allocations'). The enumeration logic itself is correct (2 sites, node_id 'gw', expected_type bool, /edges/1/condition all match the test's assertions).
per_test.fix_approach: Make freeSites also allocator.free(items) — every caller passes the result of enumerateSites (an owned toOwnedSlice), so freeSites should own and release the whole []Site. Update the function doc/comment to match the contract. Do NOT change the enumeration walker.

per_test.test: site.test.enumerateSites: timer delay -> Site with expected_type timestamp
per_test.root_cause: Same leak as the gateway test: the []Site backing from enumerateSites' toOwnedSlice is never freed (1 allocation). Enumeration logic is correct (1 site, expected_type .timestamp).
per_test.fix_approach: Same as gateway test: freeSites frees the backing slice.

per_test.test: site.test.enumerateSites: form visible_when and computed_from -> form_sites
per_test.root_cause: Same leak (1 allocation). Enumeration logic is correct (2 form sites, visible_when -> bool, computed_from -> .number via mapDeclaredTypeName('integer')).
per_test.fix_approach: Same as gateway test: freeSites frees the backing slice.

per_test.root_cause: Pure leak. isValidCelSyntax correctly rejects 'now( + 60000' (unbalanced paren), the CEL_SYNTAX_INVALID diagnostic IS emitted, node_id/expression_path are non-null — every logic assertion in the test passes. The test fails only because its defer site_mod.freeSites(...) leaks the []Site backing (site.zig:85 toOwnedSlice).
per_test.fix_approach: Same freeSites fix as the site tests. No pd06 runSyntaxCheck logic change is required for this test to pass.

per_test.root_cause: Double-free ('Invalid free' panic). The test builds TypedEnv{ .entries = entries.items } from a live std.ArrayList and defers BOTH env.deinit(alloc) and entries.deinit(alloc). TypedEnv.deinit unconditionally frees self.entries when len > 0 (it assumes ownership, transferred via toOwnedSlice / envForSite), so the ArrayList's backing buffer is freed a second time by entries.deinit. The checkSite logic itself is correct (the UnknownVariable with 'did you mean' would be produced).
per_test.fix_approach: Fix the TEST scaffolding to honour TypedEnv's ownership contract — do not double-deinit. Either (a) hand TypedEnv an owned slice (entries.toOwnedSlice(allocator)) and drop the entries.deinit, or (b) drop env.deinit and free each entry's name manually before entries.deinit. Do NOT change TypedEnv.deinit (it is correct for envForSite's owned slices).

per_test.test: typecheck.test.checkSite: '+' over number and string -> OperandTypeError
per_test.root_cause: Identical double-free to the previous typecheck test: TypedEnv{ .entries = entries.items } (borrowed slice) + env.deinit + entries.deinit free the same backing buffer twice -> 'Invalid free' panic. checkSite's arithmetic-compat logic is correct (number + string -> OperandTypeError).
per_test.fix_approach: Same as the previous typecheck test: fix the test's memory ownership, not checkSite.

per_test.test: mod.test.validateDefinition: clean linear definition with one guard -> 0 findings
per_test.root_cause: PRIMARY SIGNAL. variable_schema declares amount:number; mapDeclaredTypeName('number') returns null — the §8 table maps string/text/enum/integer/decimal/money/boolean/date/datetime/object/list<T> but NOT the plain CEL type name 'number'. Consequences, in order: (a) mod.zig emits a spurious UnknownVariableType finding for the row; (b) 'amount' is never added to the env; (c) both gateway guard sites ('amount > 0', 'amount <= 0') then emit UnknownVariable -> exactly 3 findings ('expected 0, found 3'). Empirically consistent: the leaked-allocation trace for this test shows two UnknownVariable emissions (checkSite path) plus the sites-backing leak.
per_test.fix_approach: Reconcile the declared-type table with the natural CEL type name 'number'. Preferred: add 'number' -> .number (and consider 'int'/'double') to env.zig mapDeclaredTypeName and to the accepted-set string embedded in mod.zig's UnknownVariableType message. Alternative: change the test fixtures to a mapped name (e.g. 'decimal'). CODE-DESIGNER must confirm against the design §8 table (which today deliberately omits 'number'); because .number is a first-class TypeTag in the validator and the clean-path AC expects 0 findings, extending the table is the semantically aligned fix.

per_test.test: mod.test.validateDefinition: guard references unknown identifier -> UnknownVariable
per_test.root_cause: Same 'number' not-mapped root cause as the clean-path test. amount:number is rejected, so the env is EMPTY. The guard 'amont > 0' does emit an UnknownVariable finding (saw_unknown passes), but emitUnknownVariable iterates an empty env, finds no nearest candidate and emits the no-suggestion message — so expect(saw_suggestion) fails at mod.zig:395.
per_test.fix_approach: Same as clean-path: once 'number' maps (or the fixture declares a mapped type), amount is in the env, editDistance('amont','amount')=1 <= SUGGESTION_THRESHOLD, and the 'did you mean "amount"?' message is produced, satisfying the assertion.

per_test.test: mod.test.validateDefinition: malformed CEL guard -> pd06_diagnostics populated, findings empty
per_test.root_cause: Two compounding defects. (a) PD-06 under-detection: isValidCelSyntax is a delimiter-balance-only check and ACCEPTS 'amount >' / 'amount <=' (dangling binary operator) as syntactically valid, so runSyntaxCheck returns no diagnostics and the VLD-02 AC4 short-circuit never fires -> pd06_diagnostics stays null. (b) Ordering: mod.zig accumulates env-level findings (the UnknownVariableType from the 'number' row) BEFORE the PD-06 gate, so even when the gate fires, findings is non-empty -> expectEqual(0, findings.len) fails (actual 1).
per_test.fix_approach: (a) Strengthen the per-site syntax gate so truncated/dangling-operator expressions are rejected — the correct gate is the real expr.parse (pd06.zig runSyntaxCheck per-site loop), not delimiter balance. (b) Move the PD-06 gate before any env-level finding is accumulated (or reset findings to empty on the gate path) so the AC4 short-circuit returns empty findings. Plus the clean-path 'number' mapping fix (or fixture change), which removes the spurious env-level finding.

per_test.test: mod.test.validateDefinition: findings are ordered by (node_id, expression_path)
per_test.root_cause: The test is a PD-06 gate test in disguise: it expects 'x >' / 'y <' to be malformed so the gate fires (findings empty + pd06 non-null). Because isValidCelSyntax accepts 'x >' / 'y <' (delimiter balance only), the gate never fires -> pd06_diagnostics is null -> expect(pd06_diagnostics != null) fails at mod.zig:474. The actual sortByLocation ordering logic is never reached (the gate should short-circuit first).
per_test.fix_approach: Same as the malformed-guard test's (a): strengthen the per-site gate (expr.parse-based) so truncated operators are flagged CEL_SYNTAX_INVALID. Once the gate fires, this test's assertions pass as written (findings empty + pd06 non-null). Note the ordering assertion inside it is vacuous by design (gate short-circuits); real ordering is covered by finding.zig's own sortByLocation test.

grouped_root_causes.root_cause: site.zig freeSites does not free the []Site backing slice returned by enumerateSites' toOwnedSlice -> std.testing.allocator leak-detection panic ('leaked 1 allocations')

TypedEnv.deinit unconditionally frees self.entries (ownership contract); the typecheck tests construct TypedEnv from a borrowed ArrayList.items slice and also deinit the ArrayList -> double-free 'Invalid free' panic

env.zig mapDeclaredTypeName('number') returns null (the §8 table omits the plain CEL type name 'number') -> spurious UnknownVariableType finding + the variable is absent from the env -> downstream UnknownVariable false positives
